title: Shelf publish runway: acceptance notes & sample tile copy
body:
Purpose
-----
Quick working doc for the "runway" phase of getting a Redwood Inference product tile onto cloud vendor shelves (AWS Marketplace / Azure Marketplace / GCP Marketplace). This is intentionally lightweight: acceptance scenarios + copy variants we can drop into portal forms, plus a short technical QA checklist to use with PS/Eng during final publish.

Scope
-----
- Single-sku hosted offering (hosted API product page + trial badge)
- Target vendors: AWS, Azure, GCP (notes at each acceptance step where vendor specifics differ)
- Deliverables: final tile copy (short + long), 3 screenshots captions, minimal legal hooks, SKU mapping, and test scenarios for publish smoke tests

High level runway milestones (what 'runway' means here)
--------------------------------------------------
1) Copy freeze for each vendor (short title, 80 char blurb, 400 char description)
2) Technical artifacts ready (billing SKU, trial entitlement, support contact, images)
3) Compliance quick-check (privacy, data residency note, export control)
4) Publish smoke: create listing in vendor portal, confirm preview, request sandbox purchase, validate provisioning webhook

Acceptance criteria (copy + UX)
-----------------------------
- Title: <= 60 chars, no vendor product names (e.g., "Redwood Inference Hosted API for LLMs")
- Short blurb: <= 80 chars, action-oriented, highlights 1 differentiator (latency/cost/reliability)
- Long description: <= 400 chars, includes 1 line on deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private), 1 line on SLA/uptime for Dedicated, and a link placeholder to docs
- Tile screenshot guidance: 3 images (hero screenshot, console dashboard, latency/cost graph). Each image caption must be <= 120 chars and not expose customer data.
- Trial badge: must clearly state trial length (14 days) and any usage limits; must map to internal trial SKU ID and pass billing portal smoke test
- Accessibility: alt text for all images provided
- Localization: provide short blurb translations for en, fr, de, ja (minimum)

Acceptance checklist (step-by-step)
---------------------------------
- [ ] Copy freeze (owner: Lena Park)
- [ ] Images uploaded to vendor portal (owner: Omar Ruiz)
- [ ] Billing SKU created and mapped (owner: Benji Kramer)
- [ ] Trial entitlement tested (owner: Eng - Solutions)
- [ ] Legal sign-off on data residency blurb (owner: Legal)
- [ ] Preview validated on each vendor portal (owner: Partner Ops)

Vendor-specific notes
---------------------
AWS
- Marketplace tile requires a short tagline + long description in Marketplace formatting. Also needs AMI/offer type selection when we include Dedicated bundles (N/A for just API).
- Billing: test with Metering Service sandbox purchase; ensure webhook for provisioning (internal ticket JIRA-RT-879) receives "SUBSCRIPTION_PURCHASED" callback.

Azure
- Provide 3 overview screenshots and 1 architecture diagram. Portal validates support contact email (must be a @redwood.ai address).
- Price and trial mapping happens through Microsoft Commerce APIs — coordinate with Finance to register SKU ID before preview.

GCP
- Requires a product icon 512x512 + hero 1600x800. Pub/sub-style webhook often used; confirm our endpoint accepts vendor verification header.

Sample tile copy (canonical + variants)
--------------------------------------
Note: keep variants short for A/B tile testing on vendor shelf.
Canonical title (<=60 chars): Redwood Inference — Low-latency LLM Inference API
Short blurb (<=80 chars): Production-grade LLM inference with predictable latency and usage-based pricing.
Long description (<=400 chars): Redwood Inference offers a developer-first API for running LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Ship features quickly with predictable latency, cost controls, and built-in rollouts and observability. Learn more: [docs placeholder].

Variant A short blurb: Fast, reliable LLM responses with built-in cost controls.
Variant B short blurb: Enterprise LLM serving—SLA-backed throughput and private deployment options.

Value bullets (for the portal feature list)
- High-throughput serving runtime with smart batching and KV cache
- Transparent per-token cost and token-level observability
- Dedicated capacity & private deployment options with enterprise SLAs

Screenshot captions (<=120 chars each)
1) Console: per-route latency and token-cost breakdown for a live traffic window
2) Rollouts: canary deploy UI showing traffic split and health indicators
3) Optimize: suggested batching & quantization profile with estimated cost savings

Legal & compliance blurb (short)
--------------------------------
Redwood Inference processes inference requests to deliver model outputs. Customers may choose hosted, dedicated, or private deployments; data processed in hosted deployments may traverse cloud regions as specified in your account settings. See full privacy notice: [privacy placeholder]. Questions? contact-security@redwood.ai

Technical QA checklist (smoke tests for publish)
------------------------------------------------
- Provisioning flow
  1) Create an org test account in vendor portal (or use vendor sandbox)
  2) Simulate trial purchase -> confirm marketplace sends subscription event to /marketplace/provision webhook (check timestamp + vendor signature)
  3) Our service responds 200 within 2s and creates trial record in CSDB
  4) Confirm trial usage shows up in billing UI and usage metrics start flowing

- Billing SKU mapping
  - Ensure SKU "RDW-HOSTED-TRIAL-14" maps to internal product_id "hosted_api_v1_trial"
  - Trigger a meter event from the sandbox to ensure metering arrives within 60s and increments sandbox usage counter

- Image + copy verification
  - Confirm hero image renders on preview (no CORS issues)
  - Confirm alt text appears on image tag for accessibility tools

- Smoke API call sequence (post-provision)
  - Step 1: Create API key via provisioning response payload -> confirm key creation API returns 201
  - Step 2: Call /v1/generate with prompt "smoke test" using key; expect 200 and generation latency < 1s (cold), < 150ms (warm cache) for 32-token response on hosted tier in us-west region

Open questions / unresolved
--------------------------
- Do we standardize on a single trial length across vendors (14 days) or make it vendor-configurable? (impact on billing SKU design)
- Preferred support contact: support@redwood.ai vs partner-ops@redwood.ai (Azure portal requires a single support email)
- Architecture diagram: do we want to include Dedicated flow with a simple network diagram? (legal asked to avoid showing internal IP ranges)

Quick sample metadata payload (for internal handoff to Eng/Partner Ops)
- Note: this is a text sample only — vendor portals will have form fields, we pass these values into portal UI or API

TITLE: Redwood Inference — Low-latency LLM Inference API
SHORT_BLURB: Production-grade LLM inference with predictable latency and usage-based pricing.
LONG_DESC: Redwood Inference offers a developer-first API for running LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Ship features quickly with predictable latency, cost controls, and built-in rollouts and observability.
TRIAL_SKU: RDW-HOSTED-TRIAL-14
INTERNAL_PRODUCT_ID: hosted_api_v1_trial
SUPPORT_EMAIL: partner-ops@redwood.ai
IMAGES: hero_1600x800.png, console_sample.png, optimize_tile.png
ICON: icon_512.png
LOCALES: en, fr, de, ja

Action items (next steps)
------------------------
- Omar: upload candidate images to shared drive and provide screenshot urls (due 2025-02-18)
- Benji: create billing SKU & notify Finance to register with Azure + GCP (due 2025-02-20)
- Eng (solutions): run provisioning smoke and confirm webhook flows on vendor sandbox (due 2025-02-25)
- Legal: rapid privacy blurb sign-off (due 2025-02-21)

Notes to reviewers
------------------
- This is intentionally a compact handoff doc for Partner Ops + Eng. If you have copy edits, put them inline and add a short rationale. For portal-specific constraints (max char counts, image sizes) paste a screenshot of the vendor form into this doc thread.

History / context
------------------
- Derived from prior shelf experiments (see linked artifacts) but reimagined to be an "acceptance runway" checklist — we want to reduce back-and-forth during final publish.

Misc scratchpad
---------------
- Experiment idea: tile A/B test short blurb emphasising "cost" vs "latency". Track conversion for trial creation.
- Internal note: ensure docs placeholder links map to production docs once listing goes live (do not link to staging docs).
